solution: The first ten terms are \(1,4,7,10,13,16,19,22,25,28\). Five are odd, so \[P=\frac{5}{10}=\frac12.\]
Since \(-810^\circ+x^\circ=x^\circ-720^\circ-90^\circ\), \[\sin((-810+x)^\circ)=\sin(x^\circ-90^\circ)=-\cos(x^\circ).\] Thus the answer is \(\mathrm{D}\).
Solve the two cases: \[x-7=2x+1\Rightarrow x=-8,\qquad x-7=-(2x+1)\Rightarrow x=2.\] Their sum is \(-8+2=-6\).
\[(a+bi)\overline{(a+bi)}=a^2+b^2=33,\] which is a circle centered at the origin. The answer is \(\mathrm{B}\).

Continuous compounding gives \(Pe^{0.081t}=2P\). Hence \[t=\frac{\ln2}{0.081}\approx8.56\text{ years}.\]
Matrix multiplication gives \[3a+4c=7,\quad2a-c=12,\qquad3b+4d=55,\quad2b-d=22.\] Thus \((a,c)=(5,-2)\) and \((b,d)=(13,4)\), so \[a+2b+3c+4d=5+26-6+16=41.\]
If the last of the five selected numbers is called at position \(n\), then \[P_n=\frac{\binom{n-1}{4}}{\binom{25}{5}}.\] This increases with \(n\), so it is largest at \(n=25\).

After \(d\) drops, the rent is \(950-40d\) and the number rented is \(1900+99d\). Thus \[I(d)=(950-40d)(1900+99d).\] Its vertex is at \(d=\frac{18050}{7920}\approx2.28\), so the best integer is \(d=2\), giving rent \[950-40(2)=\$870.\]

The handshake graph has \(12\) edges. Its complement has \(3\) edges. Since exactly two vertices have degree \(3\) in the original graph, the complement degree sequence is \((2,2,1,1,0,0)\), so its three edges form a path on four vertices. Of the \(\binom63=20\) triples, exactly \(3\cdot4-1-1=10\) contain a missing edge. Therefore \[P=\frac{20-10}{20}=\frac12.\]

For \(x=-t<0\) with \(t>0\), the equation becomes \[-t^9-2t^7-t^4-7t^3+6t^2-7t-9=0.\] Equivalently, \[t^9+2t^7+t^4+7t^3-6t^2+7t+9=0.\] For \(0<t\le1\), the part \(7t+9-6t^2\) is positive; for \(t\ge1\), \(t^4-6t^2+7t+9=(t^2-3)^2+7t>0\). The remaining terms are positive, so the left side is positive for every \(t>0\). There are no negative solutions, so the number is \(0\).

Write the roots as \(a,ar,ar^2,ar^3,ar^4\) and let \(A=1+r+r^2+r^3+r^4\). Then \[aA=\frac{121}{162},\qquad\frac{A}{ar^4}=242,\qquad\frac{A^2}{r^4}=\frac{14641}{81}.\] Since \(\left|A/r^2\right|=121/9\), \[\left|a^5r^{10}\right|=\left|\frac{(aA)^5}{(A/r^2)^5}\right|=\left(\frac{121/162}{121/9}\right)^5=\frac1{18^5}=\frac1{1889568}.\] The polynomial is monic of degree five, so this is \(\lvert e\rvert\).

For an arithmetic progression with \(n\) terms, common difference \(d=30/(n-1)\), and population variance \(d^2(n^2-1)/12\). Hence \[\frac{900}{(n-1)^2}\cdot\frac{n^2-1}{12}=105\Rightarrow75\frac{n+1}{n-1}=105,\] so \(n=6\). The mean is \((3+33)/2=18\), and the sum is \[6(18)=108.\]

The roots of \(x^5=1\) are \(\operatorname{cis}(0^\circ),\operatorname{cis}(72^\circ),\operatorname{cis}(144^\circ),\operatorname{cis}(216^\circ),\operatorname{cis}(288^\circ)\). The largest \(k<360\) is \(288\).

Order the three piece lengths as \(0\le a\le b\le c\) with \(a+b+c=1\). The ordered simplex has area \(1/12\). The complement of \(c\ge3a\) has area \[\int_{1/7}^{1/5}\left(3a-\frac{1-a}{2}\right)da+\int_{1/5}^{1/3}\left(1-2a-\frac{1-a}{2}\right)da=\frac2{105}.\] Thus \[P(c\ge3a)=1-\frac{2/105}{1/12}=\frac{27}{35}.\]
The period of \(\sin(2x)\) is \(2\pi/2\), so the radian period is \[\pi.\]

The triangle inequality gives \(3\le x\le27\). The cosine opposite \(x\) is \[\cos C=\frac{13^2+15^2-x^2}{2(13)(15)}=\frac{394-x^2}{390}.\] Positivity narrows this to \(3\le x\le19\), and the area condition holds throughout this range. Reducing the fraction and requiring denominator below \(37\) gives \[x\in\{7,8,11,13,15,17\}.\] Their sum is \(71\).

The displayed sequences continue by the polynomial rules, with \(t=0,1,2,\ldots\): \[k=t^3+1,\qquad w=2t^3-1,\qquad p=t^4-2t.\] For the next term \(t=6\), this gives \[k=217,\quad w=431,\quad p=1284,\] so \[k+w+p=1932.\]

The first triangle has angles \(40^\circ,40^\circ,100^\circ\). The second has angles \(30^\circ,66^\circ,84^\circ\). Thus two of the six angles measure \(40^\circ\), and \[P=\frac26=\frac13.\]
For common ratio \(r\), \(2r^4=18\), so \(r^2=3\). Since the fourth term \(2r^3\) is negative, \(r=-\sqrt3\). Therefore \[a_4=2(-\sqrt3)^3=-6\sqrt3.\]
At the positive limiting value \(k\), \[k=\frac{6k}{7}+\frac{5491}{7k}.\] Multiplying by \(7k\) gives \(k^2=5491=17^2\cdot19\), so \[k=17\sqrt{19}.\]
Because the coefficients are real, \(1-i\) is also a root. The product of the roots is \[5(1+i)(1-i)=10.\] For a monic cubic this product is \(-p\), so \[p=-10.\]

Use the tetrahedron volume formula with \(\overrightarrow{AB}=(-2,-2,-1)\), \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(-3,-1,0)\), and \(\overrightarrow{AD}=(3,3,3)\): \[V=\frac16\left|\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot(\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{AD})\right|=\frac16|-6|=1.\]
For \(k=1\), \[\frac{(x+1)!}{x!}-x=(x+1)-x=1\] for every positive integer \(x\). Thus \(k=1\).
This is an infinite geometric series with \(a=1\) and \(r=-1/4\). Hence \[S=\frac{1}{1-(-1/4)}=\frac45.\]
\(\overrightarrow{AB}=(1,2,5)\) and \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(k-1,w-4,f-3)\). Perpendicularity gives \[k-1+2(w-4)+5(f-3)=0,\] so \[k+2w+5f=24.\]

The winning strings with a run of at least three wins have counts by total wins \(3,4,5,6\) equal to \(4,9,6,1\). Therefore \[P=4\left(\frac35\right)^3\left(\frac25\right)^3+9\left(\frac35\right)^4\left(\frac25\right)^2+6\left(\frac35\right)^5\frac25+\left(\frac35\right)^6=\frac{297}{625}.\]

Set \(c=2d\). Then \[a+b=12-3d,\qquad a^2+b^2=50-5d^2.\] The condition \((a-b)^2\ge0\) gives \[-44+72d-19d^2\ge0.\] The greatest possible value is the upper root, \[d=\frac{36+2\sqrt{115}}{19}.\] Thus \(k+w+p+f=36+2+115+19=172\).
An acute angle with tangent \(1\) has equal opposite and adjacent legs. Since one leg is \(16\), the other is also \[16.\]

Let \(s=\sin A\) and \(c=\cos A\). From \(s+c=89/65\) and \(s^2+c^2=1\), the two positive possibilities are \((s,c)=(56/65,33/65)\) or the reverse. Since \(\tan A>1\), \[\tan A=\frac{s}{c}=\frac{56}{33}.\]
If \((x,y)\) lies on \(xy=324\), then \((-x)(-y)=xy=324\). The graph is symmetric about the origin, so the answer is \(\mathrm{A}\).
Divide numerator and denominator by \(x\): \[\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{20+14/x}{2+3/x}=\frac{20}{2}=10.\]
Let \(t=\log_8x\), so \(x=8^t\). The equation becomes \[8^{t^2}=\frac{8^{3t}}{8^2}=8^{3t-2},\] hence \(t^2-3t+2=0\). Thus \(x=8\) or \(64\), and the largest is \[64.\]

There are \(\binom53=10\) committees. Favorable committees have either two seniors and one junior or three seniors: \[\binom32\binom21+\binom33=6+1=7.\] Thus \[P=\frac7{10}.\]

Pascal's identity gives \[\binom{2013}{1000}+\binom{2013}{1001}=\binom{2014}{1001}.\] By binomial symmetry, the other index is \(2014-1001=1013\). The largest value is \[1013.\]

\[\frac1{n^2+3n+2}=\frac1{(n+1)(n+2)}=\frac1{n+1}-\frac1{n+2}.\] The sum telescopes to \[\frac12-\frac1{1002}=\frac{250}{501}.\]
Using \(x=1\) gives \(f(2)+3f(17)=3\), while \(x=4\) gives \(f(17)+3f(2)=18\). Solving these equations yields \[f(17)=-\frac98.\]

Equating real and imaginary parts after rationalizing gives \[\frac{3x}{34}+\frac{2y}{53}=\frac{227}{1802},\qquad \frac{5x}{34}-\frac{7y}{53}=\frac{27}{1802}.\] Solving gives \(x=y=1\). Therefore \[x^2+2xy+y^2=(x+y)^2=4.\]

The mean is \(222/11\), and the population variance is \[\frac1{11}\sum(x-222/11)^2=\frac{5166}{121},\] so \(\sigma=\sqrt{5166}/11\approx6.534\). The interval within one standard deviation is approximately \([13.648,26.716]\), containing eight entries. Thus \[P=\frac8{11}.\]

Write the arithmetic sequence as \(a-d,a,a+d\). Then \[\frac{(a-d)^3+a^3+(a+d)^3}{3a}=a^2+2d^2=81.\] With positive distinct integers, the only valid solution is \(a=7,d=4\), so the middle term is \[7.\]
The conjugate root \(1+3i\) also occurs. Since the quadratic coefficient is zero, the third root is \[-(1-3i)-(1+3i)=-2.\] The product of the roots is \(-20=-p\), so \[p=20.\]

Let \(s=\sin x,c=\cos x\). Since \(s+c=6/5\), \[2sc=\left(\frac65\right)^2-1=\frac{11}{25}.\] Also \((c-s)^2=1-2sc=14/25\), and the interval gives \(c>s\). Thus \[s=\frac{(s+c)-(c-s)}2=\frac{6-\sqrt{14}}{10}.\] Therefore \(k+w+p+q=6-1+14+10=29\).
